architecture.mechanism: Multiscale stochastic analysis of synaptic transmission to identify and quantify intermittent signal-loss steps at the molecular-to-cellular level.
architecture.intervention: Apply a multiscale stochastic diagnostic approach to the 2020 Hyundai Elantra automatic transmission by mapping intermittent torque-delivery loss (RPM flare with no acceleration) as a stochastic event chain — instrumenting torque-converter slip, line-pressure solenoid response, clutch-pack engagement timing, and TCM sensor/actuator signals at high sampling rate, then applying statistical (e.g., Markov/stochastic process) analysis to isolate the step with highest variance causing the slip.
architecture.expected_effect: Identification of the specific intermittent fault (e.g., marginal solenoid, worn clutch, contaminated fluid, or wiring/connector intermittency) even without stored DTCs, enabling targeted repair (fluid/pressure bleed, solenoid replacement, harness repair) that restores smooth acceleration and eliminates the abnormal RPM flare.
architecture.falsification_test: If, after applying the multiscale stochastic diagnostic, the transmission still exhibits RPM flare without acceleration across 10+ monitored drive cycles with no statistically anomalous step identified, or if replacing the component flagged by the analysis does not resolve the slip, the mechanism is falsified.
